name: Indus Towers Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest tower company: 270,480 towers and 440,153 co-locations (sharing factor 1.63) at Sep-2026, serving Airtel (largest tenant and ~50% shareholder, model knowledge), Vodafone Idea and Jio. Q2 FY27: revenue Rs8,516 cr (+4.0%), EBITDA Rs4,633 cr (54.4%, +0.4%), PAT Rs1,793 cr (-2.5%). Contracted, inflation-escalated revenues with energy pass-through make it a defensive dividend stock (yield 3.7%), but growth is slowing and Vi counterparty risk is the main overhang; early Africa rollouts began in 2026.

revenue_mix.segment: macro tower rentals and energy pass-through (India)

exposures.mechanism: Tower rentals are contracted, so tariff hikes act with a lag through operator health: higher ARPU supports Vi payment capacity, faster 5G loadings and lower credit-loss provisioning. Q2 FY26 had a Rs195 cr provision write-back that flattered the base (company). Roughly +10% ARPU adds ~2% to expected tenancy growth over 12m and removes counterparty-risk discount: +2.0.

evidence.note: Indus Q2 FY27 press release: revenue Rs8,516 cr +4.0%, EBITDA Rs4,633 cr +0.4%, 440,153 co-locations, sharing factor 1.63, RPT/ sharing operator -1.6% y/y

exposures.mechanism: +1 SSU = 5,000 net tenancy exits (Jio own-fibre/tower consolidation; Motilal assumes ~5,000 in H2 FY27) vs 440,153 co-locations = 1.1% of tenancies at ~100% drop-through on ~54% margin and ~20% of revenue lost carries high margin => EBITDA ~-1.9%; x EV/MCap 1.15 x persistence 0.6 = -1.3. Co-locations were +5.9% y/y but sharing revenue per operator fell 1.6% y/y (company), showing price pressure from lean/ multi-tenancy.
